gen-dafont-disorder-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta lays down ribbon-like strokes in tall, widely tracked letters, a tidy plain sans under Disorder's raw, scattered lowercase. Body text around 16px would let the spacing breathe.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-montserrat-altern: Montserrat Alternates stays crisp and rounded. Beneath it, Disorder sprawls with chaotic, widely spaced glyphs and oversized lowercase, so a 20px body size would keep the sans from being swallowed.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads like pins standing in a board, its sans-serif curves as stout as its stems. Dogica above is the heavy, wide-tracked one, with open curve ends, so a long passage here would feel steady and orderly.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-exa: Dogica leads with heavy, commanding capitals and lowercase that climbs close to them. Lexend Exa, a sans-serif drawn like a technical pen, does the quieter work of staying legible with its stubby ascenders and big x-height.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga traces each letter in flat, single-weight line, and its generous tracking gives every word room to stand apart from the next. Over a long passage it would feel modern and unhurried beneath Dogica's heavy headline.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-mega: Dogica brings heavy, commanding weight with wide tracking and clearly opened curves. Lexend Mega answers in a flat, one-nib line with a body nearly as tall as the capitals, so the two feel like a loud sign beside a friendly label.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-peta: Chunky and brash, with a friendly follow-up. Lexend Peta keeps its curves free of thinning and its big x-height tight under the ascenders, so a long passage would feel steady and approachable beneath Dogica.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, a plain sans whose open curves and stepping-stone spacing feel clean and contemporary. And Dogica, heavy and commanding, gives it a bold counterweight to stand against.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-lexend-zetta: Dogica opens heavy and commanding, with wide tracking and curves left clearly open at the ends. And Lexend Zetta carries on in neon-tube strokes of constant width, so a long passage would feel approachable and smooth.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-montserrat-alternat: Dogica's lowercase climbs nearly to its capitals. Montserrat Alternates, a plain sans with a very open c and round letters matching their stems, would make a long passage feel contemporary and lightly crowded toward the top.
